component_findings.async_structured: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Asynchronous concurrency has first-class composition and structured lifetime/join/cancellation mechanisms or an equivalent disciplined model. Evidence basis: Python | GIL prevents true multi-threaded CPU parallelism in CPython. | multiprocessing gives real parallelism but with serialization overhead. | asyncio provides native async/await cooperative concurrency, well designed for I/O-bound work. | No type-system-level data-race safety (unlike Rust). | Rich stdlib concurrency primitives (Lock, Queue, concurrent.futures) comparable to Java util.concurrent. | Structured concurrency (asyncio.TaskGroup, 3.11+) is a genuine recent improvement. | Free-threaded/no-GIL mode (PEP 703) exists but not yet default/mature. | 0-100, 100 best

component_findings.abi_calling_control: Recertified level 2 under the current criterion: ABI/calling-convention/linkage choices are explicit or safely standardized for common interoperability cases. Evidence basis: Python | CPython C-API is a first-class in-language FFI mechanism. | ctypes in stdlib allows calling shared libraries without writing C glue. | Buffer protocol (PEP 3118) enables zero-copy interop with native code. | Boxed PyObject model requires marshaling overhead vs native-ABI languages (Rust/Zig/C++). | Historically unstable binary ABI across CPython minor versions. | GIL requires explicit acquire/release around native calls for concurrency. | 0-100, 100 best
